fields.label: PART 1 - THEORY
fields.description: Written or Verbal Questions — the Candidate should answer the following questions to indicate underpinning knowledge.

fields.label: 1. The loader must be isolated with a hasp and personnel lock attached prior to entering the footprint of the machine.
2. 3 points of contact is the safest way to access and egress the loader.
3. What is the purpose of performing a walk around pre-start inspection of the loader prior to operating.
options: b) Identify any faults with the loader
c) Ensure that the loader is safe to operate

segments.optionKey: b) Identify any faults with the loader
c) Ensure that the loader is safe to operate

fields.label: 4. What action would you take if there was an “Out of Service Tag” on the loader’s isolation switch.
options: a) Ignore the tag and operate the loader
b) Remove the tag so you can operate the loader
c) Do not operate the loader and report the tag to pit control

segments.optionKey: a) Ignore the tag and operate the loader
b) Remove the tag so you can operate the loader
c) Do not operate the loader and report the tag to pit control

fields.label: 5. All working equipment at BBM is subject to a 40-metre exclusion zone.
6. The hydraulic oil, transmission fluid and coolant level on the loader can be checked by sight glass.
7. When travelling the loader, you should only use the service brake to control the loaders speed.
8. The window on the right-hand side of the cab can be used as an emergency exit point if required.
9. Prior to performing a hopper clean-up, what process would you follow.
options: b) Authorisation gained from the duty production supervisor
c) Communication with crusher control to have the orange light activated
d) Notify pit control and a general broadcast put out to all haul truck operators, notifying them of the clean-up

segments.optionKey: b) Authorisation gained from the duty production supervisor
c) Communication with crusher control to have the orange light activated
d) Notify pit control and a general broadcast put out to all haul truck operators, notifying them of the clean-up

fields.label: 10. Testing the park brake and service brake on the loader is completed in 3rd gear forward at 1700rpm.
11. When loading the bucket with material, you should only operate the loader in 1st gear.
12. Brake checks should be performed at the start of every shift, prior to leaving the park-up.
13. What action would you take if the engine oil warning light stayed illuminated once the engine has started:
options: b) Report the fault to pit control
c) Tag the loader “out of service”

segments.optionKey: b) Report the fault to pit control
c) Tag the loader “out of service”

fields.label: 14. Failure to check that the quick hitch locking pins are fully inserted, could result in the bucket attachment coming off.
15. The secondary steering system on the loader is battery operated
16. If a fire was detected on the loader that you were operating, what action would you take.
options: a) Stop the loader and ground the bucket
b) Select neutral and engage the park brake
c) Activate the fire suppression system

segments.optionKey: a) Stop the loader and ground the bucket
b) Select neutral and engage the park brake
c) Activate the fire suppression system

PART 2 – PRACTICAL DEMONSTRATION
fields.description: Materials Required: Small Loader

fields.label: 1. Plan and prepare
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Clarifies work instructions with the duty supervisor
Identify and report any potential hazards
2. Equipment Pre-Operational Checks
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Isolate the loader correctly using hasp and personnel lock
Conduct a try test prior to entering the footprint of the loader
Maintain three (3) point contact when accessing/egressing the loader
Identify & visually check external components at ground level
Identify & visually check in cab components and gauges
Check fire suppression system and fire extinguisher for condition
Check steps and handrails for condition
Check hydraulic and transmission oil sight glass for level
Check grease lines and that sufficient grease is getting to steering knuckles
Check tyres, rims and wheel studs
Check under the machine for fluid leaks
Check engine oil level on dip stick
Check windows and mirrors for condition
Complete a pre-start checklist and defect report
3. Start Up Procedure
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Check that the park brake is engaged
Adjust seat correctly and apply seat belt
Turn ignition key to the on position and visually observe monitoring system perform a self-test
Sound the horn once and wait 3-5 seconds prior to starting the engine
4. Safe Operation of the Equipment (General)
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Sound the horn twice and wait 3-5 seconds prior to moving the loader
Stop machine during transmission directional changes
Use controlled and smooth braking applications
Follow the 40m procedure while working around other equipment
Manoeuvre the loader safely and demonstrate general awareness
Demonstrate good knowledge of main road networks
Shut the loader down prior to exiting cab to ground level
5. Safe Operation of the Equipment (Mine only)
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Demonstrate/explain requirements for hopper clean up
Demonstrate good knowledge of main road networks
Follow/explain the correct procedure for clean-up (40-metre exclusion and positive radio communication)
6. Parking and Shutdown Procedures
fields.description: During the demonstration, did the Candidate:

fields.label: Ground GET and apply park brake when parking in the field and at designated parking areas
Allow the engine time to idle down
Ensure that the cab, windows and mirrors are clean
Complete the checklist and defect report
Leave cab doors and windows closed
Ensure that the engine is shut down completely before descending to ground level
Complete a post operational walk around inspection
Part 2 Assessment
fields.description: The candidate’s overall performance meets the requirements of the assessment method listed above. Sufficient performance evidence was made available during the assessment to satisfy evidence requirement of the outcome.
